details: Package name `@solana-labs/spl-toke` closely resembles the legitimate `@solana/spl-token` (missing trailing `n`, alternate scope). Pattern-level signals fire on the bundled `lib/index.cjs.js` and `lib/index.esm.js` for keyword co-occurrence (`fetch(`, `POST`, `https.get(`, `ping`), but these signals appear inside large minified bundles where the same primitives are commonly used by legitimate Solana RPC client code (POSTing JSON-RPC requests, ping/heartbeat, https GETs to documented RPC endpoints). Without traced-code confirmation that the network calls target attacker-controlled destinations or carry installer secrets, the keyword matches alone do not establish exfiltration intent. The name-similarity to a top Solana ecosystem package is the dominant concern and warrants human review for confusion-attack assessment.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
